events.title: D-Day: Allied Invasion of Normandy
events.description: Allied forces launched Operation Overlord, landing about 156,000 troops from the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and other nations on five beaches in Normandy, France (Utah, Omaha, Gold, Juno, and Sword), supported by massive air and naval operations.
events.significance: The largest amphibious invasion in history established a Western Front in Nazi-occupied Europe, and was a decisive turning point leading to the liberation of France and the defeat of Nazi Germany in 1945.

events.title: Birth of Alexander Pushkin
events.description: Alexander Sergeyevich Pushkin was born in Moscow, Russia. He would become a poet, novelist, and playwright, authoring works such as Eugene Onegin and Boris Godunov.
events.significance: Regarded as the founder of modern Russian literature, Pushkin helped establish the Russian literary language and profoundly influenced later writers such as Tolstoy, Dostoevsky, and Chekhov.

events.title: Death of Robert F. Kennedy
events.description: Senator Robert F. Kennedy died at Good Samaritan Hospital in Los Angeles, roughly 26 hours after being shot at the Ambassador Hotel on June 5, just after winning the California Democratic presidential primary. Sirhan Sirhan was arrested and later convicted of the shooting.
events.significance: The assassination, coming two months after Martin Luther King Jr.'s killing, deepened national turmoil in 1968, ended a promising presidential campaign, and altered the course of the 1968 U.S. election.

events.title: First Drive-In Movie Theater Opens
events.description: Richard Hollingshead opened the first drive-in movie theater in Camden, New Jersey, charging 25 cents per car and per person. The screen was set up so patrons could watch films from their automobiles.
events.significance: The drive-in became an iconic part of 20th-century American car culture and entertainment, peaking in popularity in the 1950s and 1960s.

events.title: Gustav Vasa Elected King of Sweden
events.description: Gustav Vasa was elected King of Sweden by the Riksdag at Strängnäs, following his leadership of the rebellion against Danish rule and the end of the Kalmar Union. This date is now celebrated as Sweden's National Day.
events.significance: His reign established Sweden as an independent, hereditary monarchy, brought the Protestant Reformation to the country, and laid the foundations of the modern Swedish state.
